meta.title: Two-Part Invention No. 2 in C minor
meta.notation_notes: 27 bars of 4/4 from quarter 0, no pickup (the subject starts after an eighth rest), no repeats. Score reconstructed from the Mutopia MIDI (Bach-Gesellschaft source, PD); notes checked against the Mutopia .ly. The .ly prall/downprall trill signs are not in the MIDI; bars 2, 4, 12, 14 and 24 carry only a written-out C–D (or G–A) turn. MIDI-derived score, not an Urtext. Two-voice counterpoint implies harmony; most half-bars carry neighbour and passing 16ths, so many spans are left as ? with the implied function in the reason.

summary: A two-voice canon in two halves. Bars 1–11: the RH subject is followed two bars later by the LH an octave below, moving from C minor to E♭ major. Bars 11–20: the same canon transposed to G minor with the voices exchanged (LH leads), moving to B♭. A two-bar sequence (21–22) leads back to C minor, where the subject returns over its own counter-line (23) and is imitated in the bass (25) before a PAC on a bare C octave.

tricks: Bars 1–11: a strict canon at the octave with a two-bar delay. One line is enough material for the whole first half.
Bar 11: the canon is restarted with the voices exchanged and transposed to G minor (invertible counterpoint); bars 11–20 mirror bars 1–10.
Bars 4–10 and 14–20: repeated ii–V7–I cells (Fm–B♭7–E♭, Cm–F7–B♭) make each relative-major key area sound settled.
Bars 22 and 24: long stepwise bass descents drive into the tonic arrivals.
Bar 27: ends on a bare C octave, leaving out the minor third.

kpop_uses.why: Bars 1–2 loop as a solo minor-key riff under a beat; add a bass on C–F–G.

review_flags.reason: E♭ read as an established modulation (bars 5–11). It could also be read as a long tonicization of III within C minor.
The arrival on beat 1 is E♭/G; G minor could be read from beat 1 (iii in E♭ = i in g). LH leader alters the subject head (E♭–F instead of G–F♯); RH follower from bar 13 is exact.
Bar 21 kept in B♭ with D7 as V7/vi; it could equally be read in g or c. Beat 4 F5 over A–D–C is left unlabelled.
Beats 3–4 contain no B♮; the cadence is labelled PAC from the bass G2–C2 and the D–C trill, not from a sounding V triad.
Final chord is a bare octave; marked ? because no third sounds. The tonic is implied.
Many spans are ? because two-voice 16th counterpoint leaves implied chords under the 70% coverage rule; each reason names the implied function.
